dedupe_keys.name: internet topology zoo over 250 operator network topologies in graphml and gml

description: The Internet Topology Zoo, published by the University of Adelaide, is a collection of more than 250 telecommunications and research network topologies transcribed from the maps operators published, stored as graphs with node geolocation and network classification. It is the standard source of realistic backbone topologies for network research, described in Knight et al., 'The Internet Topology Zoo', IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications 29(9), 2011. The original site topology-zoo.org did not answer on 26 September 2026; the authors re-deposited the data on the Adelaide figshare repository in February 2026. Coverage: national and regional backbones, research and education networks and commercial carriers on every inhabited continent, as drawn about 2010. Format and access: GraphML and GML archives (each under 1 MB), PNG maps and the source images (about 250 MB), free of charge under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the maps are snapshots from about 15 years ago; capacity and link types are often missing; the topzootools Python package is unmaintained. Simulation uses: point-of-presence level backbone graphs for resilience, cascading failure, geographic hazard exposure of fibre routes, routing and capacity planning studies. Related records: SNDlib and the CAIDA Internet Topology Data Kit give other topology views; the Telefonica and SEASON reference topologies are modern optical counterparts.
